newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends higher and over key 76.00 in May.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends higher and over key 76.00 in May.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures settled higher and over resistance at 76.00 cents basis the May contract, but analysts remained skeptical of the market's ability to hold gains.
Producer selling at the highs, they said, kept the contract below resistance for most of the session and could continue to pressure prices until higher exports are guaranteed.

"We will break through as we see a couple more weeks of strong exports," O.A. Cleveland, a cotton marketing specialist with Mississippi State University, said. "But until this market can come to terms with that, resistance at 76.00 cents is still quite strong."
The USDA will issue its weekly data Thursday at 0830 EST.

Cleveland added that several market sources expect the U.S. Department of Agriculture to eventually raise its export estimate for the 1996/97 marketing year to over 6.8 million bales from its current estimate of 6.5 million bales.
Longer-term resistance was seen at 78.00. Producer selling is likely to emerge from 77.25 cents, analysts said.
The May contract closed 0.35 cent firmer at 76.31 cents per pound, traded 76.45 to 75.75. March closed up 0.09 at 74.46 cents.
Volume was estimated at 11,000 lots, compared to Tuesday's official 17,653 lots.
